🔄 SEC Thailand NAV Auto-Sync

✓ No setup needed — reads NAV from nav-data.json updated daily by GitHub Actions.
📋 One-time GitHub Actions Setup (click to expand)
  1. Subscribe at secopendata.sec.or.th (the legacy api-portal.sec.or.th was decommissioned 30 Jun 2026) — one subscription covers both the Daily Info and Factsheet products
  2. Go to your GitHub repo → Settings → Secrets → Actions
  3. Add secret: SEC_KEY_DAILYINFO = your subscription key
  4. Add secret: SEC_KEY_FACTSHEET = same key value (one subscription, two secret names)
  5. Upload fetch-nav.js and .github/workflows/update-nav.yml to repo root
  6. Go to Actions tab → run "Update NAV Data" manually once
  7. After that it runs automatically at 9pm Bangkok time every weekday (after SEC publishes that day's NAV)

✓ Once set up, NAV updates daily with zero interaction needed.

Loading...
Debug Log
Tap "Apply NAV" to sync...
How it works: GitHub Actions runs daily at 9pm Bangkok time (after SEC publishes that day's NAV), fetches NAV from the SEC Open Data API, and saves to nav-data.json in your repo. The app reads this file directly — no CORS issues, no API keys needed in the app.

✋ Manual NAV Update

These funds are SSF/SSFE share classes whose exact NAV the SEC daily feed can't distinguish from the parent fund. Tap 🔗 Open to view the live NAV on Finnomena, read the circled price, then type the NAV and date for each fund below.

Only funds you actually hold are shown. Blank fields are left unchanged. The selected NAV Date is stamped on each saved NAV.

☁️ GitHub Gist Sync

✓ Connected · Gist ID: 64ad0078a3c2... · Last sync: 3/23/2026, 11:42:27 AM
📋 One-time Setup (click to expand)
  1. Go to github.com and sign in (free account)
  2. Go to github.com/settings/tokens/new
  3. Name it "InvestTracker", set expiry to No expiration
  4. Tick gist scope only → click Generate token
  5. Copy the token (starts with ghp_) and paste below
  6. Click Create New Gist — it creates a private Gist and saves the ID automatically
  7. Done! Data now syncs automatically across all your devices

Stored only in your browser. Never shared or baked into the HTML file.

Auto-sync: Every save (transaction, NAV, dividend etc.) auto-pushes to your Gist silently.
Opening the app on any device auto-pulls from the Gist if the cloud data is newer.
Privacy: The Gist is secret (not searchable, not public unless you share the URL). Your token never leaves your device.

⚠️ Danger Zone

Factory Reset wipes all funds, transactions, NAV history, dividends, tax savings, and local settings from this device so a new user can start fresh. By default your Gist token + ID are preserved so you can press ⬇️ Pull from Gist after reset to restore your data. Your Gist on github.com is never touched.

🔵 Google Drive

Save your HTML backups and Excel exports straight to your own Google Drive folders, instead of (or in addition to) your device's downloads.
Not connected

Create your own free Client ID in Google Cloud Console → New Project → Enable "Google Drive API" → OAuth consent screen (add yourself as a test user) → Credentials → Create OAuth Client ID → type "Web application" → add https://xneronianz.github.io as an Authorized JavaScript origin.

Anthropic/Claude never sees your Drive files or credentials — the connection runs entirely in your browser between you and Google. Uploads use Google's restricted "drive.file" permission, which only lets this app create new files in the folders you specify — it cannot read, list, or modify anything else in your Drive.

📊 Bulk Historical NAV

Backfills years of historical NAV for every fund, using the same accurate class-name-aware fetch as your daily sync. This is a heavy, occasional job — separate from the fast daily "Auto NAV" button, which stays untouched and only handles the latest NAV.

Step 1: Trigger the Action, then check your repo's Actions tab — a full 10-year fetch across all funds can take 10–20+ minutes (many paced API calls per fund), so this won't finish instantly.

Step 2: Once the workflow shows a green checkmark (it commits nav-history-bulk.json), come back and tap Apply.

What Apply does: for each date, if SEC now has data, it replaces your existing NAV with the more accurate value (using class-name filtering). Any date SEC doesn't cover is left untouched — nothing existing is ever deleted. Dates SEC has that you don't are added.

⚠️ Back up first: if Gist auto-sync is on (default), applying this will also overwrite your existing cloud backup with the new data — so it won't help you undo a bad result. Before tapping Apply, go to Settings → 💾 Backup HTML to download a snapshot to your device. That file is untouched by auto-sync and can be reopened to restore your prior data if needed.

One-time setup: upload fetch-historical-nav.js and .github/workflows/fetch-historical-nav.yml to your repo (same place as fetch-nav.js). Your GitHub Pages token needs the "workflow" scope in addition to "repo" for the Trigger button to work — add it at github.com/settings/tokens if triggering fails.

🚀 Update to GitHub Pages

✓ Deployed! https://xneronianz.github.io/investtracker (may take ~1 min to update)
📋 One-time Setup (click to expand)
  1. Go to github.com/new → create a repository named e.g. investtracker (can be private)
  2. Go to github.com/settings/tokens/new
  3. Name it "InvestTracker Pages", expiry = No expiration
  4. Tick repo scope (needed to push files) → Generate token
  5. In your repo → Settings → Pages → Source: Deploy from branch → main → /root → Save
  6. Fill in the fields below → click 🚀 Deploy Now
  7. Your app will be live at https://USERNAME.github.io/REPO

⚠ You can reuse the same token as Gist sync IF you regenerate it with both gist + repo scopes.

Your app URL: https://xneronianz.github.io/investtracker
What this does: Builds the latest HTML (with all your current data baked in) and pushes it to index.html on your GitHub repo's main branch. GitHub Pages then serves it as a live website automatically.
Privacy: If your repo is private, only people with the link can access it. Your token stays on this device only.

Fund Details

Both fields blank → this fund uses whatever's already hardcoded in fetch-nav.js, unchanged. Fund Class must be the exact, full class name from the SEC API's fund_class_name field — NOT a shortened suffix (e.g. use the whole string "K-GOLD-A(A)", not just "A(A)"). In practice this is almost always identical to the Fund Name field above, character-for-character. Leave Fund Class blank only if you've confirmed this fund's Project ID has just one share class.
